name: From Private Company to Public Company

segments.kicker: The Road to the Stock Exchange · Part 2
segments.title: From private company to public company
segments.say: Most Zimbabwean businesses start life as private companies. To list, you first have to become public. Here's how the law handles that change. This is Reian Creative Finance. Understanding markets. Following capital.

segments.title: Companies and Other Business Entities Act [Chapter 24:31]
points: Section 85 defines a private company by three restrictions
Section 86 sets out how a private company becomes public
Sections 104 to 114 cover prospectuses
Securities law and exchange rules sit on top of this
segments.say: The starting point is the Companies and Other Business Entities Act, chapter 24 31. Section 85 defines a private company, section 86 deals with becoming public, and sections 104 to 114 cover prospectuses. Securities law and the exchange's own rules then sit on top of this.

segments.title: The three private-company limits

left.head: PRIVATE (s.85)
points: Share transfers restricted
Maximum 50 members
No invitations to the public

right.head: WHY IT MATTERS
points: A listed share must trade freely
A listing needs hundreds of shareholders (300 on the ZSE main board)
An IPO is an invitation to the public

segments.note: Sources: COBE Act s.85; ZSE SI 134/2019 s.87.
segments.say: Why can't a private company list? Look at its three limits. Its shares can't move freely, but listed shares must trade freely. It can't have more than 50 members, but the Z S E main board needs at least 300 public shareholders. And it can't invite the public to buy shares, which is exactly what an I P O does.

segments.title: The conversion, step by step
steps: Board recommends the change; shareholders pass the resolution to alter the articles
Articles amended to remove the section 85 restrictions
Company stops being private from that date
Within one month: drop '(Private)' from the name
Within one month: lodge a statement in lieu of prospectus with the Registrar (unless a prospectus is registered)
segments.note: Source: COBE Act s.86. Exact resolution type: confirm with your legal practitioner.
segments.say: Here's the conversion under section 86. The board recommends the change and the shareholders resolve to alter the company's articles, removing the section 85 restrictions. From that date the company is no longer private. Within one month, it must drop the word private from its name, and lodge a statement in lieu of prospectus with the Registrar, unless it registers a full prospectus. Your lawyer will confirm the exact type of resolution required.

segments.title: A public company is held to a higher standard
points: Directors' duties and appointments: COBE Act s.195
Company secretary: functions and qualifications, COBE Act s.198
Listing rules add independent directors, committees and disclosure duties
Check the exact minimum numbers with your legal adviser
segments.note: Source: COBE Act ss.195, 198 (section locations). Specific minimums not quoted here because we could not verify them from the official text.
segments.say: A public company is held to a higher standard. Section 195 of the Act deals with directors and section 198 with the company secretary and their qualifications. Exchange rules then add expectations like independent directors, board committees and disclosure duties. We haven't quoted exact minimum numbers, because we couldn't verify them from the official text, so confirm them with your legal adviser.

segments.title: Who does what
steps: Legal practitioners: resolutions, new articles, Registrar filings
Sponsoring broker: readiness for the exchange
Company secretary: records, filings, board processes
Auditors: financial statements for the prospectus
segments.note: Practical roles; sponsoring broker requirements per SI 134/2019 ss.16–19.
segments.say: Who does the work? Your lawyers draft the resolutions and new articles and handle the Registrar filings. Your sponsoring broker prepares you for the exchange. The company secretary keeps the records and board processes in order. And the auditors prepare the financial statements the prospectus will rely on.

segments.title: Why many firms stay private
points: Founders lose some control and privacy
Every result becomes public
Compliance costs money every year
But a public company can raise capital from thousands of investors
segments.note: General considerations (interpretation by Reian Creative Finance).
segments.say: A reality check. Many Zimbabwean family businesses choose to stay private, and that can be the right choice. Going public means founders give up some control and privacy, every result becomes public, and compliance costs money every year. The reward is access to capital from thousands of investors, instead of a handful.

segments.title: Public company vs listed company

left.head: PUBLIC COMPANY
points: A legal status under the Companies Act
Set by your articles and Registrar filings
Can exist without any listing

right.head: LISTED COMPANY
points: Admitted by an exchange (ZSE, VFEX, FINSEC)
Must meet admission rules and continuing obligations
Overseen by the exchange and SECZ

segments.note: Sources: COBE Act ss.85–86; ZSE SI 134/2019; VFEX SI 62/2026.
segments.say: And don't confuse the two. Becoming public is a legal status under the Companies Act, and you can be a public company without ever listing. Being listed means an exchange has admitted your shares, and you must keep meeting its rules, under the oversight of the exchange and the Securities and Exchange Commission.

segments.title: Public back to private
points: Requires a special resolution
AND confirmation by the High Court
Delisting is a separate exchange process (Part 4)
segments.say: Going back the other way is harder. Under section 85 subsection 3, turning a public company back into a private one needs a special resolution and confirmation by the High Court. Delisting is a separate exchange process, which we cover in part four.

segments.title: Public is a status. Listed is an admission.
